common_name: Chocolate Mint Coleus (Dark Bronze Foliage with Green Edge)

planting.note: Plant transplants or rooted cuttings after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Chocolate Mint pairs deep chocolate-brown foliage with a fresh mint-green edge.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun, adjusting light exposure to what the growing conditions allow, since coleus color intensifies in brighter light but the plant scorches in the harshest afternoon sun. Chocolate Mint carries rich, deep chocolate-brown leaves rimmed in a crisp mint-green edge, a striking color combination that reads almost like a painted leaf and provides months of reliable foliage color from spring through frost. Pinch growing tips regularly to encourage bushy, well-branched growth, and remove flower spikes as they appear to keep the plant's energy directed into foliage rather than seed production.

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed in partial shade in well-drained, fertile soil or container mix; Bonfire trails readily and is a favorite for hanging baskets.

directions: Plant in partial shade in well-drained, fertile soil or container mix. Bonfire is a Bolivian begonia hybrid bearing an abundance of narrow, elongated, bright orange-red flowers that dangle from trailing stems above slender, pointed leaves, a more delicate, cascading look than the mounded habit of wax or tuberous garden begonias. Its vigorous trailing habit and continuous summer-long bloom without deadheading make it a favorite for hanging baskets and container edges, where the flowers spill dramatically over the rim. It tolerates heat better than many begonias but still benefits from consistent moisture and protection from the hottest afternoon sun.

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed in partial shade in well-drained, fertile soil; Whopper grows notably larger and more vigorously than standard wax begonias, living up to its name.

directions: Plant in partial shade to filtered sun in well-drained, fertile soil. Whopper is a landscape begonia bred for exceptional vigor, growing into a large, substantial mound of glossy foliage topped with abundant clusters of red or rose-pink flowers, filling a bed or large container far faster than standard wax begonias. Its bold scale and heavy flowering make it an efficient choice for mass plantings where quick, dense coverage is the goal. It tolerates more sun than many shade begonias if soil moisture is kept consistent, but still performs best with some protection from the harshest afternoon heat.

common_name: Big Rose Begonia (Large Green-Leaf Rose-Pink Landscape Begonia)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed in partial shade to filtered sun in well-drained, fertile soil; Big Rose is part of a landscape begonia series bred for large size and heat tolerance.

directions: Plant in partial shade to filtered sun in well-drained, fertile soil. Big Rose bears large clusters of clear rose-pink flowers over glossy green foliage on a vigorous, well-branched plant considerably larger than standard wax begonias, making it efficient for filling beds, borders, and large containers with continuous summer color. It tolerates more heat and sun than many shade begonias, provided soil moisture stays consistent, and needs no deadheading to keep flowering steadily from planting until frost. Its scale and vigor suit it well to mass landscape plantings where a big visual impact is the goal.

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed in partial shade in cool, moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil or container mix; Swingtime is a classic trailing double-flowered fuchsia grown for hanging baskets.

directions: Plant in cool, moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil or container mix in partial shade, with protection from hot afternoon sun and intense summer heat, which fuchsias tolerate poorly. Swingtime is a classic trailing fuchsia bearing an abundance of large, fully double flowers with vivid red tubes and sepals surrounding a puffy white corolla, dangling like little ballet skirts along cascading stems, a favorite for hanging baskets and porch containers for generations. It flowers most heavily in cool, humid conditions and slows or stalls in peak summer heat, so afternoon shade and consistent moisture are essential in warm-summer climates. Pinch growing tips when young to encourage a fuller, more floriferous basket, and feed regularly through the growing season to sustain its continuous bloom.
